controls.label: Color
controls.qualification: Color from Gaia's spectrum of the star. The disc is unresolved; its darker edge follows a model limb-darkening law, not a measurement.
controls.notes: The color of Gaia DR3's measured spectrum of Kepler-452. No resolved image of the surface is cast; the display axis is celestial north, a convention.

controls.label: Habitable zone
controls.notes: The star with its habitable zone drawn as a green band in the plane of its planet' orbit. The band is a calculation, not an observation: the distances at which a planet of Earth's mass with a carbon dioxide, water and nitrogen atmosphere could keep liquid water on its surface, by the model of Kopparapu et al. (2013, 2014), as the Habitable Zone Gallery (Kane & Gelino 2012) calculates them from the star's temperature and luminosity. The darker band is the conservative zone, 1.049 to 1.851 au, between the runaway greenhouse and maximum greenhouse limits; the lighter strips extend it to the optimistic zone, 0.828 to 1.953 au, between the recent Venus and early Mars limits. Planet b (1.046 au) lies in the optimistic strip inside the conservative zone. A planet in the zone is not known to be habitable.
